output.answer: Colgate-Palmolive Company has no parent company. It is itself an independent, publicly traded parent corporation — incorporated in Delaware and listed on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker CL (as of the fiscal 2025 Form 10-K, filed 2026). As the registrant in its own SEC filings, it sits at the top of its corporate group: its most recent 10-K lists the companies beneath it in Exhibit 21, "Subsidiaries of the Registrant" (e.g. Colgate Oral Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Hill's entities and other Colgate units). Ownership of its stock is dispersed among public shareholders and institutional investors — the largest being index-fund managers Vanguard, BlackRock and State Street — none of which is a controlling parent.
caveats: Large institutional shareholders (Vanguard ~10.05%, BlackRock ~8.0%, State Street ~5.79% per the 2025 DEF 14A proxy) own large blocks of stock, but these are passive fund managers on behalf of index-fund investors, not a corporate parent; their stakes change each quarter.
The list of subsidiaries in Exhibit 21 changes over time as the company acquires, restructures or dissolves entities; the version cited is as of December 31, 2025.

passages.quote: Colgate-Palmolive is a standalone publicly traded company. key_facts.fact: Colgate-Palmolive Company files its own Form 10-K with the SEC as the registrant (Commission File Number 1-644; IRS EIN 13-1815595; principal executive offices at 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10022), meaning no parent company files or reports above it.
Its common stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CL (per the 10-K cover: "Common Stock, $1.00 par value | CL | New York Stock Exchange").

Colgate-Palmolive is the parent itself: Exhibit 21 of its fiscal 2025 10-K is titled "COLGATE-PALMOLIVE COMPANY — SUBSIDIARIES OF THE REGISTRANT" and lists dozens of subsidiaries it owns, e.g. Colgate Oral Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Delaware) and Colgate (Guangzhou) Company Limited (China).

Colgate-Palmolive is "a publicly traded corporation with no single controlling owner"; it is a standalone company that is not a subsidiary of a larger conglomerate, and its largest shareholders are The Vanguard Group (10.05%), BlackRock (8.0%) and State Street Corporation (5.79%) per its DEF 14A proxy — all passive index-fund managers, not a parent.
